questions.problem:
Which of the following affine transformations are invertible?

- ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-2u-5v-9 \\ 4u+9v-9\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3u+3v+4 \\ 3u+3v-1\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3u+v \\ 8\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

The transformation is invertible if the matrix $A$ is invertible. That is, if $det(A)\ne 0.$

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is invertible. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2u-5v-9 \\ 4u+9v-9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2u-5v \\ 4u+9v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 4 & 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 \\ 4 & 9\end{aligned}|=9\cdot (-2)-(-5)\cdot 4=2\ne 0.
$$

Since the determinant is nonzero, ${T}_{1}$ is invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+3v+4 \\ 3u+3v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u+3v \\ 3u+3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot 3-3\cdot 3=0.
$$

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{2}$ is *not* invertible.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not invertible. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+v \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u+v \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}

Since the determinant is zero, ${T}_{3}$ is *not* invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1}$ only."

The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$

An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 2-1\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097781/assets/00151dc7a58722a649a52494434950695a27cb4e7cad14f32f76abbddf629a91.png)

Consider the affine transformation $T,$ given by

$$
x=u-3v+2,\,y=4v-1.
$$

What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any affine transformation 

$$
T:u⟶Au+b,
$$

where $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $u$ and $b$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors, we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., when $det(A)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., when $det(A)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $A$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $A$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a point on the plane.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

The given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-3v+2 \\ 4v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-3v \\ 4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 4-0\cdot (-3) \\  & =4 \\  & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a non-singular matrix. 

Therefore, $T$ is invertible and the image of the triangle under the action of $T$ is a triangle.

\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $\mathbf{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $\mathbf T$ gives us the following information:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097781/assets/ead1edec5d6fa82de8eb0137a838826221e0f45093782bc1b0a32111b05a37f4.png)

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot 7-(-9)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation $\mathbf{T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -9 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = -7 + 3 + 8 = 4.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
The affine transformation $\mathbf T$ is defined as

$$
x = u - v + 2, \qquad y = 4u - 5v + 9.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation $\mathbf T^{-1}$ of $\mathbf T$ is

$$
u = \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{a}x - y + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{b}, \qquad v = \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{c}x - y + 1,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $\mathbf{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+2 \\ 4u-5v+9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ 4u-5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 4 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot (-5)-(-1)\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation $\mathbf{T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-2 \\ y-9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5\cdot (x-2)+(-1)\cdot (y-9) \\ 4\cdot (x-2)+(-1)\cdot (y-9)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5x-y-1 \\ 4x-y+1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation $\mathbf{T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u = \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{5}x - y + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{(-1)}, \qquad v = \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{4}x - y + 1.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 5 + (-1) + 4 = 8.
$$
